program.description: Through the NSF Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships, APTO advances the assessment of how investments in science and technology research and development lead to changes in technology capability, production, and use. Projects study past and possible future states, create models that can extend across technology areas, and develop evidence intended to improve R&D investment decisions and strengthen long-term U.S. competitiveness.

pages.title: How technology becomes capability, production, and use
pages.introduction: The Assessing and Predicting Technology Outcomes program supports evidence, models, data sets, and tools for understanding how investments in science and technology shape technical capability, production, and use. APTO research connects historical evidence with possible future states so decision-makers can reason more clearly about research, development, and innovation.

pages.title: The teams behind APTO
pages.introduction: Meet the APTO program manager and the investigators leading each participating organization’s research. The cohort brings together universities and companies working across economic modeling, knowledge graphs, science and technology observatories, problem-focused analysis, and research-to-market translation. Organizations and people are presented alphabetically without implying rank or preference.

pages.title: Evidence for better technology decisions
pages.introduction: APTO is a National Science Foundation program building shared evidence for understanding how technologies develop, spread, and create value. Explore the participating organizations, research projects, people, and research tools for investigating technology outcomes.

pages.title: Projects across the APTO cohort
pages.introduction: Browse active NSF awards whose official titles begin with APTO. Expand a project to read its research summary, meet its investigators, visit the organization, or open the corresponding NSF award. Projects are shown alphabetically, and the map locates each participating team.

participants.name: Aperture
participants.description: Aperture develops intelligence tools that connect technical problems with relevant technologies, evidence, and organizations. Its APTO work focuses on recognizing promising opportunities and leverage points across complex research and innovation landscapes.

tools.name: Leverage Point Finder

figure.label: Opportunity signal matrix
figure.alt: Matrix comparing technical problems by evidence strength, activity, and potential leverage

tools.description: Compare technical needs, organizational activity, investment signals, and available evidence in a single ranked view. The matrix helps surface places where a focused intervention may unlock disproportionate progress.
tools.useCase: Use the finder to shortlist research questions, potential collaborators, or investment targets, then inspect the evidence behind each score before deciding where to investigate further.

tools.name: Problem Landscape Explorer

figure.label: Problem-to-solution landscape
figure.alt: Landscape connecting clusters of technical problems with technologies and organizations

tools.description: Navigate a landscape of technical problems, candidate solutions, organizations, and supporting evidence. Related needs and approaches are grouped together so gaps, crowded areas, and unexpected connections are easier to see.
tools.useCase: Use the explorer to frame an unfamiliar problem domain, find adjacent technologies, and identify organizations already working on relevant parts of the challenge.

participants.name: Insilicom
participants.description: Insilicom builds knowledge systems that turn scientific and technical evidence into structured, explorable relationships. Its APTO work connects publications, patents, databases, problems, and organizations through causal technology knowledge graphs.

tools.name: Causal Technology Knowledge Graph

figure.label: Causal technology graph
figure.alt: Directed graph connecting technologies, problems, evidence, methods, and organizations

tools.description: Explore directed relationships among technologies, features, problems, methods, datasets, and organizations. Each connection retains its supporting source so users can move from a broad systems view to the underlying evidence.
tools.useCase: Use the graph to trace possible drivers of an outcome, compare competing causal pathways, or assemble a focused evidence set for a technology assessment.

tools.name: Evidence Extraction Workbench

figure.label: Evidence extraction workflow
figure.alt: Workflow that turns articles and patents into reviewed entities, relationships, and evidence records

tools.description: Turn publications, patents, reports, and other technical text into structured evidence. The workspace combines AI-assisted extraction with human review so entities and relationships can be checked before entering a domain knowledge graph.
tools.useCase: Use the workbench to build a reusable evidence base for a new technology area, review extracted claims with subject-matter experts, and track each structured record back to its source.

participants.name: Macrocosm
participants.description: Macrocosm develops data-rich models of economic and technological systems. Its APTO work represents U.S. energy firms, physical assets, markets, investment choices, and policy feedbacks within a spatially explicit simulation environment.

tools.name: Energy System Digital Twin

figure.label: Firm and energy-asset network
figure.alt: Network of energy firms, physical assets, markets, investment relationships, and geographic connections

tools.description: Inspect a spatially explicit representation of energy firms, physical assets, local markets, and investment relationships. The model links firm decisions with technology improvement, infrastructure, employment, and materials demand.
tools.useCase: Use the digital twin to understand how a change at one firm or facility may propagate through regional markets and the broader U.S. energy system.

tools.name: Policy & Investment Scenario Lab

figure.label: Energy scenario comparison
figure.alt: Small-multiple charts comparing energy technology, policy, and investment scenarios over time

tools.description: Compare how policy choices and private investment strategies could shape energy technologies, firms, employment, and material needs. Coordinated charts make differences among scenarios visible across time and geography.
tools.useCase: Use the lab to test assumptions, compare a baseline with alternative interventions, and identify which outcomes are most sensitive to policy or investment choices.

participants.name: Northwestern University
participants.description: Northwestern University leads APTO research connecting science and technology investment with invention, licensing, company formation, and downstream outcomes. The team combines large-scale data, causal analysis, and predictive models across several technology domains.

tools.name: Research-to-Market Navigator

figure.label: Research-to-market pathway
figure.alt: Pathway from research investment through invention, licensing, company formation, and technology use

tools.description: Follow research investments through invention disclosures, licenses, company formation, and downstream technology outcomes. Linked records reveal where translation pathways accelerate, stall, or branch into different forms of use.
tools.useCase: Use the navigator to compare research-to-market pathways across institutions or technology areas and identify the stages most associated with successful translation.

tools.name: Technology Trajectory Forecaster

figure.label: Multi-technology trajectory forecast
figure.alt: Chart comparing several technology trajectories with observed values and uncertainty bands

tools.description: Compare observed and projected trajectories for technology capability, production, and use. Assumptions and uncertainty remain visible so users can see how alternative model choices change the shape and timing of each trajectory.
tools.useCase: Use the forecaster to compare candidate technologies, explore scenario assumptions, and distinguish robust signals from projections that depend heavily on uncertain inputs.

participants.name: University of Chicago

logo.sourceLabel: University of Chicago official maroon logo

participants.description: The University of Chicago team is developing a global observatory and virtual laboratory for studying how science and technology evolve. Its APTO research links research artifacts, institutions, policy choices, and technology outcomes across time and geography.

tools.name: Global S&T Observatory

figure.label: Global science and technology observatory
figure.alt: World map connecting research, patent, product, funding, workforce, and market signals among regions

tools.description: Explore how research, patents, products, funding, workforce, and markets connect across the global science and technology system. The observatory combines geographic, organizational, and temporal views of activity.
tools.useCase: Use the observatory to compare regions, trace the movement of ideas and talent, and examine how scientific activity relates to later technology outcomes.

tools.name: Virtual Policy Laboratory

figure.label: Policy experiment comparison
figure.alt: Chart comparing baseline and alternative policy scenarios for technology outcomes over time

tools.description: Run simulated policy experiments against a model of the global science and technology system. Comparable trajectories show how changes in funding, competition, collaboration, or immigration may influence later outcomes.
tools.useCase: Use the laboratory to compare policy scenarios, examine possible mechanisms, and identify assumptions or evidence that deserve closer analysis before drawing conclusions.

projects.officialTitle: APTO: A firm-level model of technological improvement, production and diffusion in the energy sector
projects.summary: Macrocosm is developing a data-driven, agent-based model of U.S. energy firms, their geolocated physical assets, and their interactions in local markets. The model is intended to explore feedbacks among technological improvement, investment, firm performance, infrastructure, and policy over the next two decades.

projects.officialTitle: APTO: Collaborative Research: Global Observatory and Virtual Laboratory for Science and Technology Advance
projects.summary: The University of Chicago team is creating a global observatory and virtual laboratory for science and technology. A chronologically trained language model will serve as a data-driven digital double of the global techno-scientific system, connecting research artifacts and metadata to measures of capability, production, and use and supporting simulated policy experiments and causal analysis.

projects.officialTitle: APTO: Constructing causal knowledge graphs for assessing and predicting technology outcomes
projects.summary: Insilicom is expanding its iKraph biomedical knowledge graph with technology entities and directed relationships drawn from publications, patents, reports, Wikipedia, and public databases. The team will also create an AI-assisted, end-to-end toolkit that APTO teams can use to extract information and construct domain knowledge graphs, including a case study in advanced manufacturing for generic drugs.

projects.officialTitle: APTO: Measuring, Understanding, Predicting, and Accelerating Technology Outcomes
projects.summary: Northwestern and its partners are building an integrated research-to-market data pipeline and predictive and causal models to measure, understand, predict, and accelerate technology outcomes. The work links university research and investment to disclosures, licensing, startups, and technology-specific measures across additive manufacturing, synthetic biology, advanced materials, AI algorithms, and therapeutics.

projects.officialTitle: APTO: Problem-Focused Analysis for Predicting Technology Outcomes and Leverage Points
projects.summary: Aperture, the platform of Artemis Intelligence, is developing problem-focused datasets that connect technical needs with technologies and organizations across selected domains. The project will mine diverse evidence sources and compare statistical signals with expert and historical ground truth to identify predictive factors, hidden opportunities, promising partners, and high-leverage research or investment targets.
